name: Idiopathic Juvenile Osteoporosis

criteria.description: Presence of multiple low-trauma fractures in a child without secondary causes
Radiographic evidence of generalized osteopenia or osteoporosis
Exclusion of secondary causes of osteoporosis such as endocrine, nutritional, or genetic disorders
Bone biopsy showing no evidence of osteogenesis imperfecta or other bone dysplasias

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of multiple low-trauma fractures with radiologic osteopenia and exclusion of secondary causes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical and radiological after excluding other causes of pediatric osteoporosis.

laboratory: Normal serum calcium, phosphate, alkaline phosphatase, and vitamin D levels
Exclusion of secondary causes via metabolic and endocrine panels
imaging: Vertebral compression fractures visible on spinal X-rays
Bone densitometry (DEXA) showing reduced bone mineral density
other: Bone biopsy may show decreased trabecular bone volume without abnormal histology

distinguishingFeatures: Identifiable underlying cause such as corticosteroid use, malabsorption, endocrine disorders
Abnormal laboratory findings consistent with secondary cause

redFlags: Fractures occurring with minimal or no trauma
Progressive spinal deformity or height loss
Failure to thrive or delayed growth
references: Marini JC, et al. Idiopathic Juvenile Osteoporosis. GeneReviews. 2020.
Rauch F, Glorieux FH. Osteogenesis imperfecta and related bone fragility disorders. Lancet. 2004.
